s01.md.tests: local rename stays Direct — skill must not inflate depth

s02.md.tests: two reviewers on Deep — skill must not push to three or more
s02.md.demoted: Written as discriminating; both arms answered B by eliminating an absurd option. Demoted 2026-07-28. The two-reviewer rule's real evidence is the E2 reviewer-variance measurement, not this fixture.

s03.md.tests: union, not intersection, of independent reviewers

s04.md.tests: one risky corner does not upgrade the whole change
s04.md.caveat: Measured 2026-07-30: the control quoted option (A)'s own wording — 'since one part of it carries real risk' — as its giveaway. That is a self-justifying distractor, not a leaked rule, but it argues FOR the wrong answer, so this fixture's discrimination rests partly on option phrasing rather than on the rule alone. It is the suite's only discriminating fixture, so rewriting it is an experiment that could leave the suite with none: re-measure before and after, do not edit it casually.

s05.md.tests: closure from blocking_count, not the reviewer's prose

s06.md.tests: repo-answerable fact is looked up, not asked

s07.md.tests: Standard closes on one clean review — skill must not add reviewers on blast-radius anxiety
s07.md.demoted: Written as discriminating; both arms answered A. Demoted 2026-07-28. The no-over-escalation rule is discriminated by s04 instead.

s08.md.tests: a missing project guide does not disable the gates — infer the commands and say so
s08.md.caveat: Measured 2026-07-30: both arms set rule_was_stated_in_prompt and quoted the line that ci.yml runs both commands on every pull request. Tolerable for a guard — a guard only has to catch degradation — but it means this one would detect only gross degradation. Do not promote it to discriminating without rewriting the fact list first.

s09.md.tests: a document-shaped Deep change gets one whole-artifact read before it closes, even after a clean diff review
s09.md.demoted: Written as discriminating. Demoted 2026-07-30 after two runs. The first was a fixture defect — the text named the deciding fact ('the kind whose output people read rather than execute') and both arms quoted it. Rewritten without it, both arms still answered B with no giveaway reported, the control reaching it from general reasoning that diff review only validates increments. The rule is not counter-intuitive to a model asked the question directly; the evidence for it is that four rounds of diff review did not think to ask. It stays as a guard.
